hints.title: Platform Classification Matrix
hints.text: A user active on both mobile and desktop on the same date belongs to the both platform category.

hints.title: Cartesian Date-Platform Grid Union
hints.text: Generate all combinations of spend_date with desktop, mobile, and both, then left join user daily platform classifications.

hints.title: Purchase Platform Blueprint
hints.text: Determine per-user daily platform (mobile, desktop, both). Generate date-platform grid from distinct dates and platforms. Left join and aggregate total amount and user count.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH UserDaily AS (
    SELECT spend_date, user_id,
           CASE 
               WHEN COUNT(DISTINCT platform) = 2 THEN 'both'
               ELSE MAX(platform)
           END AS platform,
           SUM(amount) AS total_amount
    FROM Spending
    GROUP BY spend_date, user_id
),
Dates AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT spend_date FROM Spending
),
Platforms AS (
    SELECT 'desktop' AS platform UNION ALL
    SELECT 'mobile' UNION ALL
    SELECT 'both'
),
Grid AS (
    SELECT d.spend_date, p.platform
    FROM Dates d
    CROSS JOIN Platforms p
)
SELECT g.spend_date, g.platform,
       IFNULL(SUM(u.total_amount), 0) AS total_amount,
       COUNT(u.user_id) AS total_users
FROM Grid g
LEFT JOIN UserDaily u
  ON g.spend_date = u.spend_date
 AND g.platform = u.platform
GROUP BY g.spend_date, g.platform;
```

complexity.notes: User daily grouping followed by cross join grid left aggregation runs in linear-logarithmic time.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Omitting missing platforms on dates with 0 activity drops mandatory zero-filled rows from the final report.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Cross join grid guarantees all three platform categories are emitted for every active calendar date.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of CROSS JOIN date-platform grid and COUNT(DISTINCT platform) = 2 conditional classification.

import pandas as pd

def user_purchase_platform(spending: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    grouped = spending.groupby(['spend_date', 'user_id']).agg(
        platforms=('platform', set),
        amount=('amount', 'sum')
    ).reset_index()
    def get_plat(p_set):
        return 'both' if len(p_set) == 2 else list(p_set)[0]
    grouped['platform'] = grouped['platforms'].apply(get_plat)
    agg_user = grouped.groupby(['spend_date', 'platform']).agg(
        total_amount=('amount', 'sum'),
        total_users=('user_id', 'count')
    ).reset_index()

    dates = spending['spend_date'].unique()
    grid = []
    for d in dates:
        for p in ['desktop', 'mobile', 'both']:
            grid.append({'spend_date': d, 'platform': p})
    grid_df = pd.DataFrame(grid)
    res = grid_df.merge(agg_user, on=['spend_date', 'platform'], how='left')
    res['total_amount'] = res['total_amount'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    res['total_users'] = res['total_users'].fillna(0).astype(int)
    return res
solutions.approach: Pandas Cross Product Grid with Aggregated Left Merge
